quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Swimming ___ great exercise for your whole body.
quests.completedSentence: Swimming is great exercise for your whole body.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Swimming' is a gerund acting as the subject, and gerunds are always treated as singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Swimming' names one single activity here, even though it's something people do many times.
quests.example: Swimming is great exercise for your whole body.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Reading ___ one of my favorite ways to relax.
quests.completedSentence: Reading is one of my favorite ways to relax.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Reading' is a gerund subject, so it's singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Treat this -ing word as one single activity, just like 'swimming'.
quests.example: Reading is one of my favorite ways to relax.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Cooking ___ a lot of patience and practice.
quests.completedSentence: Cooking requires a lot of patience and practice.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Cooking' is a gerund subject, so it's singular. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Cooking' names one single activity, no matter how many dishes it involves.
quests.example: Cooking requires a lot of patience and practice.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Learning a new language ___ years of consistent practice.
quests.completedSentence: Learning a new language takes years of consistent practice.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Learning a new language' is a gerund phrase functioning as one singular subject. The verb takes -s: 'takes'.
quests.nativeTip: The whole phrase 'learning a new language' acts as one subject - find where it ends.
quests.example: Learning a new language takes years of consistent practice.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Waking up early every morning ___ me feel more productive.
quests.completedSentence: Waking up early every morning makes me feel more productive.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Waking up early every morning' is a gerund phrase, treated as singular. The verb takes -s: 'makes'.
quests.nativeTip: Even though this phrase is long, it still describes one single activity.
quests.example: Waking up early every morning makes me feel more productive.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Playing video games for hours ___ his eyesight, according to his doctor.
quests.completedSentence: Playing video games for hours strains his eyesight, according to his doctor.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Playing video games for hours' is a gerund phrase and counts as one singular subject. The verb takes -s: 'strains'.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the entire activity being described, not just the last word before the verb.
quests.example: Playing video games for hours strains his eyesight, according to his doctor.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Collecting stamps ___ his main hobby.
quests.completedSentence: Collecting stamps is his main hobby.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Collecting stamps' is a gerund phrase and is singular, even though 'stamps' is plural. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Stamps' is plural, but it's not the subject - the whole gerund phrase is.
quests.example: Collecting stamps is his main hobby.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Fixing old cars ___ a special kind of patience.
quests.completedSentence: Fixing old cars requires a special kind of patience.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Fixing old cars' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Cars' is plural, but the real subject is the whole activity, which is singular.
quests.example: Fixing old cars requires a special kind of patience.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Organizing large events ___ careful planning and teamwork.
quests.completedSentence: Organizing large events demands careful planning and teamwork.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Organizing large events' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'demands'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Events' is plural, but don't let that distract you from the true subject.
quests.example: Organizing large events demands careful planning and teamwork.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To exercise regularly ___ important for long-term health.
quests.completedSentence: To exercise regularly is important for long-term health.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: An infinitive phrase like 'to exercise regularly' is treated as singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'To exercise regularly' describes one single goal, so treat it as singular.
quests.example: To exercise regularly is important for long-term health.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To travel abroad ___ one of her lifelong dreams.
quests.completedSentence: To travel abroad is one of her lifelong dreams.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To travel abroad' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: This infinitive phrase names one single dream, even though it involves visiting many places.
quests.example: To travel abroad is one of her lifelong dreams.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To finish this project on time ___ our top priority.
quests.completedSentence: To finish this project on time is our top priority.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To finish this project on time' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The whole 'to' phrase acts as one single subject here.
quests.example: To finish this project on time is our top priority.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To master several languages ___ years of dedication.
quests.completedSentence: To master several languages takes years of dedication.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To master several languages' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'takes'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Languages' is plural, but the infinitive phrase as a whole is still singular.
quests.example: To master several languages takes years of dedication.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To visit all seven continents ___ her ultimate travel goal.
quests.completedSentence: To visit all seven continents is her ultimate travel goal.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To visit all seven continents' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Continents' is plural, but focus on the entire infinitive phrase instead.
quests.example: To visit all seven continents is her ultimate travel goal.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To answer these questions correctly ___ careful thought.
quests.completedSentence: To answer these questions correctly requires careful thought.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even when it contains a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To answer these questions correctly' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Questions' is plural, but the true subject is the whole infinitive phrase.
quests.example: To answer these questions correctly requires careful thought.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'that' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: That she always arrives early ___ everyone at the office.
quests.completedSentence: That she always arrives early surprises everyone at the office.
quests.grammarRule: A 'that' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That she always arrives early' is a 'that' clause functioning as the subject, and it's singular. The verb takes -s: 'surprises'.
quests.nativeTip: An entire 'that' clause can act as the subject of a sentence, and it's always singular.
quests.example: That she always arrives early surprises everyone at the office.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'that' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: That he forgets important dates ___ his wife more than anything.
quests.completedSentence: That he forgets important dates bothers his wife more than anything.
quests.grammarRule: A 'that' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That he forgets important dates' is a 'that' clause and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'bothers'.
quests.nativeTip: Treat the whole idea introduced by 'that' as one single subject.
quests.example: That he forgets important dates bothers his wife more than anything.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'that' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: That the plan might fail ___ a real possibility.
quests.completedSentence: That the plan might fail remains a real possibility.
quests.grammarRule: A 'that' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That the plan might fail' is a 'that' clause and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.nativeTip: This 'that' clause describes one single possibility, so it's singular.
quests.example: That the plan might fail remains a real possibility.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: What she says ___ everyone in the room.
quests.completedSentence: What she says surprises everyone in the room.
quests.grammarRule: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'What she says' is a 'what' clause functioning as the subject, and it's singular. The verb takes -s: 'surprises'.
quests.nativeTip: A 'what' clause works just like a 'that' clause - one idea, one singular subject.
quests.example: What she says surprises everyone in the room.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: What the manager decides ___ final.
quests.completedSentence: What the manager decides is final.
quests.grammarRule: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'What the manager decides' is a 'what' clause and is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The whole idea introduced by 'what' counts as one singular subject.
quests.example: What the manager decides is final.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: What they discovered ___ the whole investigation.
quests.completedSentence: What they discovered changes the whole investigation.
quests.grammarRule: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'What they discovered' is a 'what' clause and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'changes'.
quests.nativeTip: Even though 'discovered' suggests a big finding, the clause itself is still one singular subject.
quests.example: What they discovered changes the whole investigation.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Exercising every day ___ your energy levels.
quests.completedSentence: Exercising every day improves your energy levels.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Exercising every day' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'improves'.
quests.nativeTip: This subject is a gerund phrase - recall the rule from earlier in this stage.
quests.example: Exercising every day improves your energy levels.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To learn a musical instrument ___ years of daily practice.
quests.completedSentence: To learn a musical instrument takes years of daily practice.
quests.grammarRule: Infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To learn a musical instrument' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'takes'.
quests.nativeTip: This subject starts with 'to' - which type of subject is that?
quests.example: To learn a musical instrument takes years of daily practice.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'That' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: That the team missed the deadline ___ the whole department.
quests.completedSentence: That the team missed the deadline worries the whole department.
quests.grammarRule: 'That' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'That the team missed the deadline' is a 'that' clause and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'worries'.
quests.nativeTip: This subject is introduced by 'that' - remember how that type of clause behaves.
quests.example: That the team missed the deadline worries the whole department.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund phrase stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Learning to code, especially at a young age, ___ many career opportunities.
quests.completedSentence: Learning to code, especially at a young age, opens many career opportunities.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund phrase stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Learning to code' is the true gerund subject; 'especially at a young age' is a parenthetical aside. The verb takes -s: 'opens'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase between the commas is just an aside - the gerund phrase itself is still the subject.
quests.example: Learning to code, especially at a young age, opens many career opportunities.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To finish the marathon, despite the extreme heat, ___ an incredible achievement.
quests.completedSentence: To finish the marathon, despite the extreme heat, remains an incredible achievement.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To finish the marathon' is the true infinitive subject; 'despite the extreme heat' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.nativeTip: Skip over the phrase about the heat and connect the infinitive subject directly to the verb.
quests.example: To finish the marathon, despite the extreme heat, remains an incredible achievement.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'that' clause stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase inside it
quests.sentenceWithBlank: That the results varied so much, even after three attempts, ___ the researchers.
quests.completedSentence: That the results varied so much, even after three attempts, puzzles the researchers.
quests.grammarRule: A 'that' clause stays singular, even with an interrupting phrase inside it
quests.ruleExplanation: The whole 'that' clause, including the aside about three attempts, is still one singular subject. The verb takes -s: 'puzzles'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase about the number of attempts is just extra detail inside the 'that' clause.
quests.example: That the results varied so much, even after three attempts, puzzles the researchers.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Reading before bed ___ me fall asleep faster.
quests.completedSentence: Reading before bed helps me fall asleep faster.
quests.grammarRule: A gerund used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Reading before bed' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'helps'.
quests.nativeTip: Bring back the gerund rule from earlier in this stage.
quests.example: Reading before bed helps me fall asleep faster.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: To admit a mistake ___ real courage.
quests.completedSentence: To admit a mistake takes real courage.
quests.grammarRule: An infinitive phrase used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To admit a mistake' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'takes'.
quests.nativeTip: Remember the infinitive rule: one goal, one singular subject.
quests.example: To admit a mistake takes real courage.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: What she accomplished ___ everyone on the team.
quests.completedSentence: What she accomplished inspires everyone on the team.
quests.grammarRule: A 'what' clause used as the subject takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'What she accomplished' is a 'what' clause and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'inspires'.
quests.nativeTip: As a final check, treat this 'what' clause as one singular idea.
quests.example: What she accomplished inspires everyone on the team.
